sentence: This project maps changes in mitochondrial DNA across brain regions and blood to learn how they relate to Alzheimer's disease and cognitive decline.
This project builds a sequencing test that finds drug resistant tuberculosis directly from samples without growing the bacteria in culture.
This project tests in a clinical trial how a fatty acid supplement changes metabolism in preterm infants.
This project tries to find out how the cell machinery of human neurons helps misfolded tau clumps spread in Alzheimer's disease.
This project prepares scientists to work on environmental health problems using genomics, exposomics and very large data sets.
This project studies why T cells respond differently to tumors in men and women and how male hormones weaken that response in bladder cancer.
This project builds a heart attack on a chip model to study how low oxygen changes communication between the main cell types in the heart.
This project builds large protein language models that use protein structure and function to make better predictions about protein properties.
This project tries to find out how glioblastoma cells change their surroundings to escape attack from immune cells, using laboratory models.
This project studies genetic causes of primary aldosteronism in Black Americans and looks for treatments that block aldosterone production driven by mutations.
This project studies how Merkel cell carcinoma escapes the immune system and tests combination treatments for patients whose tumors resist current immune therapy.
This project selects biomedical pilot research projects from faculty at partner colleges and guides the project leaders as they carry them out.
This project generates sequencing and metabolite data to study how bacteria, their phages and gut microbes shape infections by antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
This project brings scientists together to discuss what different types of myeloid cells do and how they could be used in treatments.
This project studies how exposure to the pesticide dieldrin changes gene methylation and how that may lead to Parkinson's disease.
This project tries to find out which regulators control communication between cells in the bone marrow so that it can regrow after stem cell transplantation.
This project develops faster imaging and motion-robust methods so children with inflammatory bowel disease need less anesthesia during MRI scans.
This project uses a radiotracer to test whether alpha-synuclein clumps in the brain can tell apart Parkinson's disease, Lewy body dementia and multiple systems atrophy.
This project builds a renewable human liver model to study hepatitis B and hepatitis C infection and how genetic variants change the course of disease.
This project builds ways to track HIV variants that are rising in Central Asia so that spreading clusters can be detected earlier.
